The implementation is complete and thoroughly validated. Summary of what was done:

**Implementation** (`/app/submission/main.py`, ~30 KB, stdlib only):

1. **Strict JSON Lines reader** â reads all of stdin, splits on newlines, enforces the 32 MiB per-line bound (E_LIMIT), strict parsing (duplicate keys, `NaN`/`Infinity`, non-finite float overflow, invalid UTF-8 â E_JSON), plus a per-line exception net so no traceback ever reaches stdout and processing continues.

2. **Three-schema validation** â E_SCHEMA (unknown/missing keys, wrong types incl. booleans, non-rectangular arrays, duplicate triples/actions/slot-seqs/ranks), E_LIMIT (all numeric-range, string-length and collection-size bounds), E_JSON (syntax level).

3. **`replay`** â exact bounded-switch model: circular slot buffer with absolute tags, `floor`/`up_next`/`acked`, both ACK paths, retry timeouts in increasing-`q` order (over the wrapped ring), storage-aggregation rules, full-entry `down` broadcasts, negative ACKs on out-of-window arrivals, missing/drop/duplicate handling, and the 2048-pending / 200000-creation caps (whole-request E_LIMIT).

4. **`audit`** â safety over the reachable states with a shortest BFS-constructed prefix to any unsafe state; fair-termination via a line-graph (edge-marking) reduction with an EmersonâLei style SCC-elimination fixpoint (weak = generalized BÃ¼chi over *disabled-state âª internal a-edge*, strong = Streett pair), which correctly handles fair subcycles inside an SCC whose strongly-fair exits leave it. Counterexamples are built as prefix + closed walk, growing the walk by the cheapest internal fairness edge (or a-disabled state) one bit at a time, bounded well under the 1 000 000 edge-ID budget; pure-stutter lassos use the implicit `-1` edge.

5. **`export`** â lossless `ModelData` TLA+ module with the eight required constants in order, ASCII-sorted 1-based action indices, all explicit edge triples, WF/SF index sets, and per-state safe/done sets, plus the exact config tokens.

**Verification**: public examples pass; differential fuzzing against an independently written brute-force liveness oracle (all state subsets, up to 13 states) and an independently written replay simulator (random and protocol-driven event streams, >10 000 cases) reported zero mismatches; export output was validated against an independent parser for every fuzzed case; maximum-size inputs (12 000 states / 60 000 edges / 16 fairness conditions / 29 MB lines / 20 000 events) run in â¤2 s.
